$comment: docs/localization.md §L9.4 — every ICU argument that carries a user or technical value into a localized sentence, and the isolate it takes. A value entering through an ICU ARGUMENT has no element to carry `dir`, so markup cannot reach it. Each site names the resolved KEY SET, the argument slot and the isolate kind; `scripts/check-isolate-arguments.mjs` asserts all three against the AST.
$address: A site is addressed by (file, enclosing function, RESOLVED KEY SET). That one address covers every shape: a literal key is a one-member set, a computed key is an n-member set, and two calls sharing a key are two entries. The previous schema needed a `keyAuthority` special case per shape and C3.5 added three more — a local `const` holding a conditional, an inline conditional, and a map lookup with a `??` fallback.
$limit: This manifest defends the call sites listed here, exactly and in both directions. It does NOT by itself discover a NEW ICU argument that starts carrying a user value later — that half is `scripts/check-icu-arguments.mjs`, which enumerates EVERY ICU argument in shipped source and refuses one that is neither mechanically classifiable nor dispositioned. The two together close the population; neither alone does. `scripts/content-direction.json` still carries the original unbounded limit, because a new text-rendering ELEMENT is a different question and only a census finds that.
$history: PR B recorded 11 decision rows and deferred them. C3.5 re-ran the population from the TypeScript type checker — 205 ICU arguments — and found 27 more that carry user or technical values: 8 in its first pass (the unrecognized-column header and the five `import.loc.*` calls) and 19 that its first pass only RECORDED as open. All 27 are implemented here, so no row of the disposition manifest is classed `auto`, `ltr` or `per-fragment` any more.

obligations.carries: the user's own TABLE LABELS, comma-joined into one ICU argument
obligations.why: A single isolate around the joined list would give the whole list one paragraph direction, taken from whichever table the user happened to name first. MEASURED in PR B: two of six cases broke identically with and without that single isolate. Each label is isolated on its own; the quotes and the comma stay OUTSIDE, because they are the sentence’s punctuation and not the label’s.

obligations.carries: the user's spreadsheet COLUMN HEADER, on the two events that name an EXISTING column
a USER CELL, display-formatted
obligations.note: THREE recorded rows, ONE producer: `issueText` is called at three render sites and holds one catalog call. The key is not written in the source at all — it is `ISSUE_KEY[issue.code]`, which `resolveKeys` resolves to the map’s 27 values, and the ARGUMENT is prepared before the call rather than written in an object literal, so the wrap is asserted over the assignment.

obligations.carries: the user's spreadsheet COLUMN HEADER (the key column)
obligations.lineage: NOT lost. Recorded pre-PR-B as one concatenated expression, `keyText + " · " + t("import.status.counts", {cols,rows,n})` at :864. C3 split that JSX child into three children, so the recorded expression no longer exists as written; the obligation moved to the producer `keyText`, whose header-carrying branch is this call. It also NARROWED — the `import.status.counts` half interpolates only numbers.

obligations.carries: the user FRAME NAME, at the head of a localized sentence
obligations.note: The sr-only accessibility path. Nobody can see it, which is exactly why it needed recording rather than dropping.

obligations.carries: a NODE ID — a technical token whose direction is known in advance
obligations.why: `LRI` and not `FSI`: an id starting with a digit or a symbol has no strong character of its own, so a first-strong isolate would hand it the surrounding paragraph’s direction.

obligations.carries: RAW document values via `rawOrDash`
obligations.note: TWO recorded rows, ONE producer: `groupLine` is one catalog call rendered at two JSX sites (the editable path and the read-only path). TWO arguments, both isolated.

obligations.carries: a shortened revision identifier — generated, direction known
an INCOMING spreadsheet column header the refresh did not recognise
obligations.why: The direct peer of `refresh-column-header`, in the same file and the same list, carrying the same kind of value — the PR B census recorded the two events that name an EXISTING column and not the one that names a NEW one. Nothing distinguished them but which side of the refresh the header came from.

obligations.carries: the user's TABLE NAME and, on two branches, the COLUMN HEADER
obligations.why: `issueText` renders `${issueLocation(issue)}: ${desc}` — ONE string. `desc` already isolates its `{value}`; without these the same sentence carried one bounded argument and two unbounded ones, and the two unbounded ones came first.

obligations.carries: a user SPREADSHEET TABLE name, in the dialog heading the modal is named by
a user SPREADSHEET TABLE name, looked up from the dependent table id
a user CELL value — the incoming and the existing foreign key
a NODE ID with an optional offset (`@id`, `@id + 3`), or a bare number on the literal branch
obligations.why: `String(...)` is safe here and was measured rather than assumed: a bare `{n}` is NOT number-formatted by intl-messageformat, so a number and its string render identically, in `ar` and `ar-EG` alike. The literal branch is wrapped too — a digit run has no internal order to break, and one direct wrap is what the checker can assert exactly.

obligations.carries: a user PARAMETER label, falling back to a node id
obligations.why: `auto` and not `ltr` because the PRIMARY value is free text whose direction is not known in advance; the id fallback is the exception, not the rule.

obligations.carries: a NODE ID, in the four unresolved-activator sentences
obligations.note: The key is a local `const key` whose initializer is a three-deep conditional of four literals. `resolveKeys` resolves it to that closed set; before C3.5 the checker could only resolve a literal or a named map.

obligations.carries: a user-typed RESOURCE TYPE name, after normalisation
several INDEPENDENT user RESOURCE TYPE names, joined into one argument
obligations.why: The same shape as `canvas-import-hint-tables`. EACH type is isolated, not each pair and not the join: the `↔` between a pair and the `, ` between pairs are the sentence’s, so one isolate around the whole list would give every name the direction of whichever one came first.

obligations.carries: two language ENDONYMS from the registry (`nativeName`)
obligations.why: Foreign script BY CONSTRUCTION — the endonym for Arabic is Arabic and for Japanese is Japanese — and the banner is rendered in whichever language is still active, so the sentence and the value routinely disagree. This is the one site where the value’s direction is not merely unknown but usually opposite.

obligations.carries: a user PARAMETER label (`labelOf(...) || refId`)
obligations.why: The two node labels in the SAME row are isolated with markup (`<bdi dir="auto">`) — PR B took those. This one enters through an ICU argument in the sibling span, where markup cannot reach it, and was missed because it is not in the element the census ruled.

obligations.carries: a user REGISTER/PARAMETER name — the node a reference cycle runs through
obligations.note: The reference listbox renders this as TEXT. The same key built inside `candidateName` is an `aria-label` instead, and stays on the attribute axis (`scripts/icu-argument-disposition.json`).

obligations.address: The enclosing is the COMPONENT, not `errText`: that arrow is wrapped in `useCallback`, so neither checker names it a function, and both address it the same way. The key set is what distinguishes this site from the other three in the same component.
obligations.carries: a user NODE name OR a node id, depending on which row the diagnostic code selects
obligations.why: TWO kinds on ONE CALL SITE: `{name}` is free user text and takes `FSI`, `{id}` is a generated token and takes `LRI`. Declaring a single kind per obligation would have forced the wrong one on one of them. Note what this is NOT: no single catalog value uses both — `regExpr.row.wrongKind` interpolates only `{name}` and `regExpr.row.unknownRef` only `{id}` — so a rendered sentence carries one isolate, not two. The call passes both because the key is not known until runtime.
obligations.note: The key is `REF_ROW_KEY[r.code] ?? 'regExpr.row.generic'` — a map lookup with a literal fallback, which `resolveKeys` unions.

obligations.carries: a user NODE name, announced after a reference is inserted
a user NODE name carried on the arm hint
obligations.note: TWO call sites with the SAME key in the same function — the polite live region and the inline hint paragraph. The site schema addresses them as two entries sharing one key set, which the previous one-site-per-key rule could not express.

obligations.carries: a shortened REVISION ID — `shortId` strips `rev_` and takes six characters, exactly what `RevisionChip` does
obligations.note: The key is an INLINE conditional of two literals. The whole expression is wrapped rather than only the id branch: the em-dash placeholder is a technical token too, and one direct wrap is what the checker can assert exactly.
